# API reference

Layers: **code is the source of truth** for names, signatures and behavior; these generated pages carry the technical detail (symbols, signatures, parameters, CLI options); conceptual contracts stay manual in [pipeline](../pipeline.md), [projects](../projects.md), [exports](../exports.md), [viewer](../viewer.md) and [manual edits](../manual-edits.md); step-by-step workflow and operating limits stay in `.agents/skills/`.

## Public vs internal

Public (stable, documented here): `lib.__all__`, `Tools.TexturePainter.__all__`, the `Tools.TexturePainter.ink` builders (`Path`, `line`, `curve`, `bezier`, `arc`, `vertices`, `boundary`, `stroke`, `style`), `Tools.TexturePainter.looks` (`Look`, `Pass`, `LayerStyle`, `Overlay`, `Region`, `Style`, `PaintLayer`, `paint_looks`), `Tools.TexturePainter.theme` (`Theme`, `define_theme`, `load_theme`), `Tools.recipe_context` (`RecipePaths`, `recipe_paths`, `recipe_environment`), `Tools.uv_builder.UVBuilder`, and the `Tools.forge` commands.

Internal (importable but not stable, intentionally absent): `lib` submodules (`primitives`, `procedural` helpers, `geometry_types` internals, validation, `spatial` helpers beyond `__all__`), including the mesh-construction cores (`loft`, `sweep`, `segment`, `revolve`, `segment_sections`, `sweep_sections`), `MeshFace` and `box_surface_contacts` — prefer the `ModelBuilder.add_*` constructors; `Tools` implementation modules (`_resolve`, `project_manifest`, `recipe_emit`, `gltf_export`, `low_poly_audit`, `uv_contract`, `uv_builder` internals, `viewer_server`, `TexturePainter/core`), including `TextureExporter` and the painter color helpers, and the `Tools.*` re-export in `Tools/__init__.py`, which covers only a subset — import painter symbols from `Tools.TexturePainter`.

Ambiguities (conservative choice): `Tools.uv_packer.BoxUVPacker` is used by tests but recipes and skills use `UVBuilder`, so only `UVBuilder` is public; direct `py -m Tools.<stage>` invocations work, but `Tools.forge` is the canonical CLI; `AnimationEditor(path, source, data)` constructs from internals — use `AnimationEditor.from_bbmodel()`.
